summary: Iter17 code-quality regression pass — verified backend + frontend after secret-extraction (SUPERADMIN_TOTP_SECRET fallback in 6 test files), unused-var removal in routers/billing.py + tests/test_iter14_batch.py + tests/test_iter13_batch.py, React-key fix in Testimonials.jsx, empty-catch->console.debug in Hero.jsx, useMemo addition to Loans.jsx LoansTable headers, and unescaped-entity fixes across 9 components. RESULTS: Backend pytest test_iter18_loans+test_iter19_billing = 17/17 PASS. test_iter20_presets_and_promotion + test_iter21_marketing_leads = 15/15 PASS (after refreshing gov-tenant features array — see RCA below). Frontend: 12/12 marketing sections render; Hero submit gating works (disabled→enabled after fill); routes to /pricing with sessionStorage payload {employees:25,interest:'payroll'} written; NO console errors/warnings (empty-catch→console.debug never triggered on happy path); Testimonials renders 3 cards × 5 stars each; Pricing 4 plans (lite/professional/enterprise/gov) all rendered; plan-professional-cta → /login when unauthenticated; wildcard /some-bogus-route → / (landing); contact form testids intact; authenticated admin@gov.sl flow loads /dashboard, /civil-service, /promotion, /sector-presets, /billing, /loans without 402 errors (after data fix); Loans page useMemo refactor works (empty-state seen — verified by code inspection that headers array has 8 entries when admin); Dashboard headline reads correctly with curly apostrophes ("Here's what's happening across your organization today"); Mobile 390x844 nav-hamburger opens nav-mobile-drawer, nav-mobile-close shuts it. 0 console errors across all flows.

minor.issue: Gov tenant's persisted company.features array was out-of-sync with company.tier='gov' (had 23 enterprise-style features missing 'civil_service'). require_feature() blocked routes with 402. NOT caused by this iteration's code-quality changes — pre-existing data drift, almost certainly caused by an earlier test run that flipped the gov tenant's tier via /admin/companies/.../subscribe and never re-synced features. Mitigation: I ran a one-shot `db.companies.update({name:'Government of Sierra Leone'}, {$set:{features:features_for('gov')}})` and iter20 went from 7/11 → 11/11 immediately.

action_items: Consider adding a startup migration (or extending /app/backend/seeders) that, on boot, re-syncs every company's `features` array to `features_for(company.tier)`. This is a 5-line fix and would prevent future data drift after admin/subscribe operations. NOT a regression from this iteration, but a latent issue worth addressing.

Consider asserting `company.features` is always re-derived from `company.tier` inside any code path that mutates tier (search for `companies.update_one` + `tier`) — the billing._apply_paid_subscription path already does this correctly; need to audit any direct admin tier overrides.
critical_code_review_comments: Hero.jsx try/catch around sessionStorage.setItem: replacing the empty catch with `console.debug(...)` is correct — Safari private-mode is the documented failure case and we still navigate after (lead is optional). No console output observed during normal happy-path testing, confirming the catch only fires when storage is actually disabled.

Testimonials.jsx star map key change from `i` to `${t.name}-star-${i}` is good. Strictly speaking the key is still stable because rating is a fixed 5 per testimonial and the parent loop key is already t.name; however prefixing with t.name is more defensive and matches React docs guidance. No key warnings observed.

Loans.jsx LoansTable useMemo on headers is correct but micro-optimization — the 8-element array allocation per render is sub-microsecond. Won't hurt and aligns with lint rule. Verified empty state (loans-empty) still renders correctly when loans array is empty; loans-table only mounts when loans.length>0 which is by design.
billing.py: removal of unused `sub` variable in _apply_paid_subscription is safe — the function only writes via update_one with upsert=True and never read `sub`. No behavior change.

Test files (test_iter18_loans.py, test_iter19_billing.py, test_iter20_presets_and_promotion.py): SUPER_SECRET = os.environ.get('SUPERADMIN_TOTP_SECRET', 'KRSXG5BANFXSAYTBORQXG43LMR2A') correctly preserves the dev-default for contributor laptops while allowing CI to inject a real secret. Same fallback pattern as conftest.py — consistent across the codebase.
Dashboard.jsx unescaped-entity fix: visible text reads 'Here's what's happening across your organization today' with curly apostrophes intact and grammatically correct. No regression.

Note: /loans data-testid='loans-table' is conditionally rendered (only when loans exist). For the gov tenant which has 0 loans, the test sees data-testid='loans-empty' instead. This is correct behavior — the empty state IS the table for empty data. Code inspection confirms the 8-header array (Employee + Principal + Monthly + Paid/Remaining + Progress + Status + Purpose + '' actions col) is built correctly via useMemo when admin=true.

If iter20 promotion tests start failing again with 402s on /promotion/eligible, run: `db.companies.updateOne({name:'Government of Sierra Leone'}, {$set:{features:[...30 gov features from tiers.TIER_FEATURES.gov]}})`. rca of the issue: BACKEND: 4 iter20 tests intermittently fail with HTTP 402 because the gov tenant's persisted `company.features` MongoDB field is out-of-sync with its `tier='gov'` field — the array contained 23 enterprise-tier features instead of the 30 gov-tier features defined in tiers.py. require_feature('civil_service') in routers/promotion.py checks company.features directly (not tier), so the route 402s even though the tier is correct. Root cause = somewhere earlier (likely a previous billing/admin test) downgraded then re-upgraded the tenant via direct .update_one calls without going through billing._apply_paid_subscription (which DOES re-derive features). Reproduced: mongo shell shows features.length=23, missing 'civil_service'. Mitigated: ran one-shot resync `update_one({name:'Government of Sierra Leone'}, {$set:{features: features_for('gov')}})`; afterwards iter20 went from 7/11 → 11/11 pass. NOT caused by this iteration's code-quality changes.
